findings.why_it_matters: The PDF prints 3.1 as a numbered subsection heading on its own line, the same style as 3.3 and 3.4 on page 720, which the markdown renders as '## 3.3 ...' and '## 3.4 ...'; here it is a plain paragraph, so the subsection is invisible to heading-based navigation (informative History of COBOL appendix).
Same as p719-1: the numbered subsection heading 3.2 is left as a plain paragraph while its siblings 3.3 and 3.4 (page 720) are markdown headings (informative History of COBOL appendix).

The PDF prints 4.3 as a numbered subsection heading, the same style as 4.1 and 4.2 on page 722, which the markdown renders as '### 4.1 ...' and '### 4.2 ...'; here it is a plain paragraph (as are the errata-inserted 4.4 and 4.5 headings on the same page), so the subsection is invisible to heading-based navigation (informative History of COBOL appendix).
